title: Personalized Baseball Uniforms (2026)
verdict: For personalized baseball uniforms in 2026, choose Wooter. Every player gets a jersey and pants in their own sizes with their own name and number, and the roster that drives it is entered once.

Boombah does the same job well for jerseys and pants. Champro personalizes through its dealers. Custom Ink personalizes tops only. Nike Team adds names and numbers to stock uniforms within three weeks.

ranking.fit: Teams that want each player's uniform right the first time: name, number, jersey size and pants size.
ranking.lacks: Three to four weeks from approval. A late roster change means a second order.

ranking.fit: Baseball teams that want sublimated jerseys and pants from one maker's own factories.
ranking.lacks: Its baseball pages quote different lead times. Get the date in writing.

ranking.fit: Teams with a local dealer that want a cut-and-sew Juice jersey or a lower-cost Splash one.
ranking.lacks: Ordered through a dealer account, with lead time confirmed after artwork approval.

ranking.fit: Programs happy with a stock Nike uniform personalized with names and numbers.
ranking.lacks: Stock designs only on the faster option.

ranking.fit: Rec and company teams that need a printed button-front jersey in about two weeks.
ranking.lacks: Stock garments with your print added, not a jersey built from your pattern.

why: Personalizing a uniform is harder than personalizing a jersey. Each player has two sizes, and a twelve-year-old's jersey size tells you little about his pants.
Wooter treats the two separately. The roster holds a jersey size and a pants size per player, and copying the roster from jersey to pants keeps names and numbers in step.
Sizing kits are available if you want the team to try pieces on before the order.

criteria.name: One roster
criteria.text: Entered once and copied across pieces.

criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.text: A proof that shows every name and number.

criteria.name: Additions
criteria.text: A way to add a player mid-season.

faq.q: How do we collect everyone's sizes?
faq.a: Use a sheet with name, number, jersey size and pants size. A sizing kit removes the guessing.

faq.q: What if two players want the same number?
faq.a: Settle it before you order. The roster will accept duplicates, and the umpire will not.

faq.q: Can we add a player later?
faq.a: Yes. The design is on file and the minimum is one on most items.

faq.q: Do names go on the pants?
faq.a: Usually not. A number on the hip or a logo on the leg is more common.
Wooter's product pages quote three to four weeks from design approval, and rush production is available.
